epic.title: Improve GCSP matching and release performance
epic.description: Reduce avoidable matching and persistence work as employee, car and release history volumes grow, so releases stay responsive while preserving eligibility, preference ranking, deterministic fleet allocation and explainable history. Deliver the source-derived improvements in independently reviewable User Stories estimated at no more than eight points each. Keep the existing behaviour and authoritative transaction safeguards. Context: docs/gcsp/presenter-release-db-diagnosis-2026-11-11.md; related FUCQ-177 and FUCQ-247. Added by: Russell Gowers (authored with Codex)

stories.title: Resolve allocation stock rows through an order-ID index
stories.goal: As a presenter, I want releases to resolve matching stock efficiently as the available pool grows.
stories.decided: Build the order-ID index once for the current visible pool. Hoist simple per-employee invariants only where existing guards stay identical.
ac: Eligible decisions resolve the same stock row, revision and provenance, in the same deterministic contender order, using direct order-ID lookup.
Missing or ambiguous contract dates block exactly the same otherwise-eligible decisions; ineligible decisions do not acquire new blockers.
A bounded synthetic case demonstrates lookup construction plus candidate lookups grows linearly with pool and candidate count, replacing the repeated available.find scan.
stories.out: Decline history indexing, allocation policy changes, ranking changes and persistence redesign.
stories.description:
goal:

stories.title: Consume pending triggers without replaying unchanged history
stories.goal: As a presenter, I want each release to process new or unfinished allocation work without replaying unchanged completed triggers.
stories.decided: Use story 11's bounded indexed reads for durable consumption/provenance state. Resume pending claims before new triggers.
ac: Only new, changed or unfinished triggers need processing; unchanged completed history does not repeatedly replay allocations.
Crash/restart, uncertain commit, repeated delivery and pending attempts preserve idempotency and exactly the existing authoritative claim semantics.
Changed payloads under a completed producer identity still conflict; an unchanged producer-supplied digest alone is never trusted, and legacy data follows a safe validation path.
Consecutive-release and native PostgreSQL recovery cases demonstrate bounded processing with equivalent offers and audit references.
stories.out: Dropping history, assuming exactly-once event delivery, replacing the scheduler or changing release policy.

stories.title: Batch PostgreSQL evidence hydration within memory bounds
stories.goal: As a scheme operator, I want selected history results reconstructed with fewer database round trips and bounded memory.
stories.decided: Batch only evidence digests referenced by the supplied selected rows. Bound response/materialisation bytes as well as digest count; preserve the current protection against large configurations.
ac: Reconstructed results preserve row order, legacy inline evidence, digest verification and fail-closed missing/corrupt-evidence behaviour.

Many small snapshots use bounded batches rather than one query per distinct digest; mixed or oversized snapshots remain within declared working-set limits and oversized values travel individually without truncation.
No unbounded parallel queries or full evidence-table reads are introduced; native PostgreSQL tests show equivalent results and fewer round trips.
This works with the existing row selection and does not depend on new revision, write-set or selected-receipt features.
stories.out: Schema revision, history deletion, general transaction hydration redesign and storing copied inputs in validation outputs.
